coverage: Reported geographical segments · segment revenue before inter-segment revenue
definition: Each region's profit from its operations before depreciation, other income, interest, exceptional items and tax, as the segment note presents it. The rows add up to ₹3,156.23 crore, which becomes profit after tax of ₹1,861.47 crore once those items and tax are taken off. It is not profit after tax.
location: Annual and integrated report 2025–26, PDF page 471 (printed page 471), consolidated statement of profit and loss; PDF pages 547–549 (printed pages 547–549), note 51 segment reporting; PDF page 521, note 36 exceptional items; PDF pages 552–553, note 56 prior period adjustment
notes: Figures are reported in ₹ crore and are not converted. The segments are regions, not products: India, Indonesia, Africa (which the filing says includes Strength of Nature, a subsidiary in the USA) and Others. Segment revenue of ₹15,427.84 crore is before ₹249.94 crore of inter-segment revenue; revenue from operations after removing it is ₹15,177.90 crore. From segment result of ₹3,156.23 crore the filing adds other income ₹82.03 crore and interest income ₹184.14 crore, and takes off depreciation and amortisation ₹267.52 crore, finance costs ₹331.57 crore and exceptional items ₹233.15 crore, to reach profit before tax of ₹2,590.16 crore; tax of ₹728.69 crore leaves profit after tax of ₹1,861.47 crore, all belonging to the company's owners. Tax includes a ₹36.91 crore prior-period adjustment. Exceptional items (net cost of ₹233.15 crore) are: restructuring costs ₹80.70 crore (severance pay in Latin America, Africa and India); Labour Codes ₹44.82 crore (extra retirement-pay and leave provisions under India's new labour laws); litigation costs ₹44.11 crore at Strength of Nature in the USA, including a class action over its hair relaxer products; litigation settlement ₹29.47 crore in Indonesia and Ghana; loss on sale of a subsidiary ₹28.26 crore; acquisition costs for the Muuchstac brand ₹15.59 crore; less a reversal of an investment write-down ₹8.82 crore and a ₹0.98 crore fall in contingent consideration payable. The company restated last year's revenue: it now deducts amounts payable to customers from revenue instead of showing them as expenses, with no effect on profit (note 56). No single customer brought in 10% or more of revenue. The company does not disclose profit for any single brand or product.
insight: India earns most of the segment result, and Indonesia earns a higher result on each rupee of revenue than Africa does. Because the rows are regions, these figures cannot show which products make the most profit.
